# Hydra ETL

> Hydra ETL is an open-source (AGPL-3.0, commercial license available) declarative ETL engine for Python 3.9+. Pipelines are described in YAML, validated before any data is read or written, and run from a CLI (`hdrctl`), a REST API or a visual editor (Hydra Studio), all installed with `pip install hydra-etl`. Latest version: 0.19.0 (November 4, 2026), beta.

Key facts:
- A project holds jobs (one source, an ordered list of transformations, one destination: four YAML files), workflows that chain jobs and actions, and `workflows/thread.yaml`, the order in which workflows run (sequential or parallel stages, delays, loops). `hdrctl run <project>` checks the whole project before running anything.
- Connectors: CSV, JSON, Parquet, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, SQL Server, MongoDB, Web API. 20 transformations, including join (inner, left, right, outer, cross), aggregate, window functions and text_to_rows.
- Engines: pandas by default; DuckDB + pyarrow for large volumes (20 million rows aggregated in 34 s instead of 113 s, same results as pandas), chosen per job with `engine:`; optional Rust acceleration.
- Reliability: all-or-nothing load per job, workflow rollback (`rollback: true`, `undo:` on actions), fallback workflows (before the start or after a failure, only if nothing was published), timeouts per workflow.
- Triggers (`triggers.yaml`, since 0.19): cron, interval, file arrival, marker file, source change, webhook with token, end of another project. Run by `hdrctl watch` or `hdrctl serve`.
- Sub-projects (since 0.19): a workflow step `type: project` runs another project, with cycle checks and results readable by the next steps.
- Parameters, environments and secrets: `parameters.yaml`, `environments/<env>.yaml`, global variables in `~/.hydra/env`, secrets in `.hydra/secrets` or encrypted with SOPS, masked in every log.
- Ships an MCP server so AI assistants can write and check pipelines, and a VS Code extension with schemas and snippets.

## Docs

- [Get started](https://hydraetl.com/get-started/): what Hydra ETL is and your first job
- [Install](https://hydraetl.com/install/): `pip install hydra-etl`, extras and troubleshooting
- [Hydra DSL reference](https://hydraetl.com/dsl/reference/): the YAML manifest language
- [Guide](https://hydraetl.com/guide/): every source, destination, transformation and workflow element
- [CLI tutorials](https://hydraetl.com/cli/): create, validate and run jobs with `hdrctl`
- [Studio tutorials](https://hydraetl.com/studio/): build jobs visually
- [VS Code extension](https://hydraetl.com/vscode/): completion and validation for manifests
- [Changelog](https://hydraetl.com/changelog/): every release, dated, with its new features and fixes
